outcome: Antimicrobial susceptibility of B. gladioli isolates
cohort: 2,676 newborns in the neonatal intensive care unit in Putian City, Fujian Province, China, from 2011 to 2014.
finding: B. gladioli infection was found in 3.25% of newborns, with a higher prevalence in premature infants, and while it was sensitive to many antibiotics, it may be a potential causative agent for bacteremia in neonates.
